manifest.name: dsh-opencode-session-fallback
manifest.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: give session-less LLM requests on OpenCode routes a fallback session id, so auto-review stops failing with 400 MissingSessionID.
manifest.author: zlxlsy666

readme.text:
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-opencode-session-fallback)
[](./LICENSE)

A small [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) plugin that gives
**session-less LLM requests** on OpenCode routes a fallback `sessionId`, so `auto` permission presets stop
failing every tool call with `400 MissingSessionID`.

No global `fetch` patching, no provider config changes, no official package overrides.

OpenCode / OpenCode Go reject inference requests that do not carry an `x-opencode-session` header:

```
400 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"MissingSessionID","message":"Request is missing x-opencode-session ..."}}
```

DSH's `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` adapter only lets pi-ai add that header when the request carries a
`sessionId`. Main conversation calls do carry one — but
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-auto-review` builds its **reviewer request by hand without a `sessionId`**.

So with the `auto` permission preset on an `opencode-go` route:

1. every tool call is first sent to the reviewer model,
2. that request has no session header → gateway 400,
3. the review fails → DSH fails closed → the tool body never runs:

```
Auto review of tool "pwsh" failed; its body was not executed:
auto-review: reviewer ended with error INVALID_REQUEST: 400: {"type":"MissingSessionID", ...}
```

Wrap `ctx.llm.stream` once at startup. Requests that already carry a `sessionId`, or that target a
provider outside the configured list, pass through untouched. Only **session-less requests on OpenCode
routes** (in practice: the auto-review reviewer call) get the configured fallback id; pi-ai then adds
`x-opencode-session` on its own.

```
ctx.llm.stream(options)
  ├─ options.sessionId present .......... pass through (main chat, subagents, compaction, titles)
  ├─ provider not opencode/opencode-go .. pass through (official DeepSeek etc. untouched)
  └─ session-less + OpenCode route ...... { ...options, sessionId: <fallback> }

Why not patch `globalThis.fetch` (what some other plugins do)? Because replacing the global `fetch` wraps
**every** outbound call of the host — including the app's own networking — and can take the whole UI down
with connection errors. This plugin only touches the LLM service method.

- Existing `sessionId`s are **never** replaced → per-conversation routing / prompt-cache affinity is preserved.
- Other providers (for example the official `deepseek` provider) are **not affected at all**.
- Options objects passed by callers are **never mutated** (a copy is used, so frozen options are fine).
- Uninstalling restores the original `ctx.llm.stream` automatically.
- If the service shape changes in a future DSH release, the plugin logs a warning and stays inert instead of
  breaking the boot.
> Plugins are assembled at DSH startup — **restart DSH after installing**.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-opencode-session-fallback
```

Or use the GUI: **Settings → Plugins → install**, package name `dsh-opencode-session-fallback`.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/zlxlsy666/dsh-opencode-session-fallback.git
```

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "file:C:\path\to\dsh-opencode-session-fallback"
```

The desktop application manages its own `desktop` profile: use its **Plugin Manager** UI for that profile
instead of the CLI.

After a successful start the log shows:

```
[opencode-session-fallback] active for providers [opencode, opencode-go], fallback session id "dsh-opencode-session-fallback"
```

Override with the same entry id in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: opencode-session-fallback
  name: dsh-opencode-session-fallback
  config:
    providers: [opencode, opencode-go]    # routes that need a session id

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-opencode-session-fallback
```

Restart DSH afterwards.

- Built and verified against DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` (desktop) with `opencode-go` + `deepseek-v4.1-flash`,
  where it fixed the failure end-to-end (auto preset, tools execute, reviewer returns normal allow/deny
  decisions).
- Requires `ctx.llm.stream` to exist (`inject: ['llm']`); otherwise the plugin logs a warning and does nothing.
- Pairs well with any DSH version that ships the pi-ai OpenCode providers.

```sh
node --check lib/index.js
node test/smoke.mjs   # 5 assertions, no DSH runtime required
```

MIT

---

OpenCode / OpenCode Go 要求每个推理请求都带 `x-opencode-session` 头，缺失会返回
`400 MissingSessionID`。DSH 的 `dsh-llm-pi-ai` 只在请求带 `sessionId` 时才让 pi-ai 补这个头，而
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-auto-review` 的 reviewer 请求是手工拼的、**没有 sessionId**。

结果：在 `opencode-go` 路由 + `auto` 权限预设下，每次工具调用先过 reviewer → reviewer 请求 400 →
审查失败 → fail-closed → 工具全部无法执行。

启动时包一层 `ctx.llm.stream`：

- 已有 `sessionId` 的请求（主对话、子代理、压缩、会话标题）**原样透传**；
- 其他 provider（例如官方 `deepseek`）**完全不受影响**；
- 只有「缺 sessionId 且命中 OpenCode 路由」的请求（实际就是 reviewer）补一个兜底 id，
  pi-ai 随后自动加上 `x-opencode-session`。

**不接管全局 `fetch`**（那会把宿主自身的出网调用一起包住，可能直接让 UI 报 connection error），
也不修改 provider 配置、不覆盖任何官方包。

插件在 DSH 启动时装配，**装完必须重启 DSH**。

- npm：`dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-opencode-session-fallback`
- GUI：设置 → 插件 → 安装，填包名
- Git：`dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/zlxlsy666/dsh-opencode-session-fallback.git`
- 本地目录：`dsh plugin --profile web add "file:C:\path\to\dsh-opencode-session-fallback"`

桌面版的 `desktop` profile 由应用自己管理，请在应用的插件管理器里安装。

启动日志应出现：

```
[opencode-session-fallback] active for providers [opencode, opencode-go], fallback session id "dsh-opencode-session-fallback"
```

在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 用同 id 覆盖：

```yaml
- id: opencode-session-fallback
  name: dsh-opencode-session-fallback
  config:
    providers: [opencode, opencode-go]

从插件管理器卸载（或 `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-opencode-session-fallback`）后重启 DSH，
`ctx.llm.stream` 会自动恢复。

DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` 桌面版 + `opencode-go` 路由 + `deepseek-v4.1-flash`：修复后 auto 预设下工具正常执行，
reviewer 能正常返回 allow/deny 决策。
